chapters.title: A swarm with different priorities.
chapters.body: Bugs arrive inside your viewport near the pointer. Small bugs stay near local food and buttons. Grown hunters keep their assigned mission, biting letters already in their path. Scrolling can outrun the swarm; attached bugs track their target geometry while free bugs retain their document position.

chapters.title: The button is a living health bar.
chapters.body: The first bite fades the button to mint green. Yellow starts at 75% health, then coral red at 35%. Damage drains a fill behind the real label. Desktop surfaces ripple and bubble; mobile uses stable native CSS gradients and quiet radial bubbles. The label, icon and original handler remain part of the host page.

chapters.title: Rescue is a decision, not a teleport cheat.
chapters.body: Offscreen attack alerts offer Jump from 50 points and Jump + Zap from 200. Each rescue increases the jump and zap prices; each zap increases its own price further. A zap clears a limited radius and awards only one point per kill. Manual scrolling is always free.

chapters.title: Optimization without rewriting the game.
chapters.body: Swarm keeps its established engine. A reusable Range and a nearby glyph shortlist constrain geometry work. The navigation audit preserved full deterministic gameplay and DOM traces while reducing ancestry checks by 81.8% and distance calls by 90.4% in the documented workload. Those are operation counts, not an FPS claim.

site.extra: Optional hidden activation: ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A Enter. A deferred entry can wait for load, delay and idle before installing the activation bootstrap; the game itself loads on first open or start.

characters.name: Cursor target
characters.rules: Move the crosshair over a bug and click to hit it. On touchscreens, tap the bug directly. Larger bugs can take more than one hit.

characters.name: Crawler
characters.rules: Starts with one hit point. Feeds on real letters, changing each bite to 0 or 1. Squash it before it grows.

characters.name: Evolved crawler
characters.rules: After six letters it grows and gains one hit point. Earlier damage still counts; evolution does not fully heal it.

characters.name: Button hunter
characters.rules: After twelve letters it grows again and gains one more hit point. It hunts buttons, bites text on the way, and drains button integrity.

page.lead: Release a swarm onto this page, then defend it. Bugs eat letters into binary, grow stronger and drain your buttons. Squash them before the interface falls apart. It plays right here in your browser: no install, and Recall gives the page back.
page.support: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

howToPlay.title: Release the swarm
howToPlay.body: Press Play. The bugs arrive in your viewport, near the pointer.

howToPlay.title: Squash the bugs
howToPlay.body: Click or tap a bug to squash it. Bugs that have eaten grow stronger and can take more than one hit.

howToPlay.title: Save the buttons
howToPlay.body: Bugs eat letters into 0 and 1, grow, and hunt the page's buttons. Squash them before the buttons lose their colour.

howToPlay.title: Rescue distant attacks
howToPlay.body: When bugs attack a button off screen, an edge alert offers Jump from 50 points or Jump + Zap from 200. Scrolling there yourself is always free.

howToPlay.title: Recall the page
howToPlay.body: Press Escape or Recall to end the round and restore the page.

tips.title: Scroll to outrun them
tips.body: Scrolling can outrun the swarm, and it never costs points.

tips.title: Rescues get pricier
tips.body: Every rescue raises the Jump and Zap prices by 25 points, and each zap adds another 150. Prices reset on restart.

tips.title: Zaps don't pay
tips.body: A zap clears a 140–220 px radius around the destination but returns only 1 point per kill, with no combo multiplier.

tips.title: The secret code
tips.body: On sites that install the hidden activation, ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A Enter opens the game.

strategy.title: Squash crawlers before six letters
strategy.body: A crawler has one hit point. After six letters it grows and gains a hit point, and after twelve it becomes a button hunter with one more. Every early squash saves you hits later.

strategy.title: Damage sticks
strategy.body: Evolving does not fully heal a bug: hits it took before it grew still count. Finish wounded bugs first.

strategy.title: Triage by colour
strategy.body: A button fades to mint green on its first bite, turns yellow at 75% health and coral red at 35%. Defend the red buttons first.

strategy.title: Scroll before you pay
strategy.body: Scrolling is always free and can outrun the swarm. A Jump costs 50 points and Jump + Zap 200, and every rescue raises both prices by 25.

strategy.title: Zap only to save a button
strategy.body: A zap clears a 140–220 px radius but pays 1 point per kill with no combo multiplier, and each zap adds another 150 to its price. Use it when a button is about to fall, not to farm points.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything to play Swarm Protocol?
faq.a: No. Swarm Protocol plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and press Escape or Recall when you are done to give the page back.

faq.q: Can I play Swarm Protocol on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. Tap a bug to squash it. Phones keep a steady fill and lighter effects.

faq.q: What happens to the page when I play?
faq.a: Bugs eat the page's letters into 0 and 1 and drain the colour from its buttons. Recall restores what the game changed and still owns.

faq.q: Can I put Swarm Protocol on my own site?
faq.a: Yes. It is open source (MIT), as an npm package or a self-hosted drop-in ZIP. Your visitors never load it from GitHub or a game server.
